title: Console: Compact Insights MVP — scope pruning and staged rollout plan
creator: Aisha Patel
description: PRD refactor: produce a trimmed, testable slice of Console Insights for launch while preserving core developer value. This ticket captures the intentional cuts, rationale, acceptance criteria, and a staged rollout and rollback plan so we can ship an MVP that gives product teams actional cost and latency signals without the full dashboard surface or advanced trace viewer.
background: Stakeholders requested a smaller, shippable surface to hit an internal milestone and reduce OSS/infra scope. Original PRD covered a wide set of cards (end-to-end request flows, per-token cost models, heatmap timeline, full trace flamegraph, per-route cost breakdowns). Engineering constraints (runtime instrumentation bandwidth, backend aggregation compute, and data retention costs) force scope reductions to meet the target date. This ticket enumerates the cuts, the reasoning, and compensating controls (feature flags, progressive enhancement) to minimize regresion risk.
scope_changes: REMOVE: Full trace flamegraph viewer (defer to next quarter) — keep trace table with top-5 sampled spans
REDUCE: Dashboard card set cut from 12 to 6 core cards (see card_list_reference)
SIMPLIFY: Cost breakdown to a single 'route-level' drilldown endpoint rather than per-token micro-breakdowns
DEFER: Historical long-tail retention (90d) — keep 14 day retention for MVP; add retention toggle in roadmap
ADD: Canary feature flag to gate advanced tracing and per-token cost endpoints for dedicated customers only
card_list_reference: Error budget burn and SLO indicator
KV cache hit rate and effective token savings
Recent significant regressions (auto-detected via prompt sets)
acceptance_criteria: Dashboard loads in under 1.2s (cold) for accounts with <= 100k monthly requests using default aggregation windows
Six core cards render with correct data and CTA links to troubleshooting docs
Trace table shows sampled traces with span-level durations; flamegraph endpoint responds with 202/acceptance when requested (feature-flagged) — flamegraph UI is not shipped
Cost breakdown API returns route-level daily buckets for last 14 days and matches billing report within 3% for test dataset
Feature flagging implemented: advanced-trace and per-token-cost default off; manual enable for staging and dedicated customers
Canary rollout plan documented and automation in CI to flip flags for 5%/25%/100% cohorts
QA regression checklist completed: dashboard edge cases (zero-traffic routes, cold cache), sampling bias verification, and synthetic load tests
Monitoring: SLO alerts for dashboard error rate (>=1%) and backend aggregation latency (>2s) created and tested
rollout_plan: Stage 1: Internal dogfood — feature flags on for internal org only; validate performance and data accuracy (2 days)
Stage 2: Limited external beta — enable for 3 pilot customers on Dedicated (1 week)
Stage 3: Gradual public rollout using 5%/25%/100% cohorts with automatic rollback on alert conditions
Rollback criteria: dashboard error rate >1% sustained for >10min OR cost-breakdown API latency >2s for 5+ consecutive minutes
tradeoffs_and_notes: We accept reduced historical retention to lower storage and aggregation cost and ship sooner; this degrades long-range trend visibility for customers but preserves immediate operational signals
Removing flamegraph reduces frontend complexity and storage; retains trace table so SREs can still identify root causes via sampled traces
Per-token cost accuracy requires heavy instrumentation; route-level attribution gives useful guidance with 80–95% of value at a fraction of cost
Will ship with clear messaging in Console 'What's included' and in customer release notes to set expectations
